ety.text: Borrowed from Sanskrit अभिनेतृ (abhinetṛ). By surface analysis, अभि- (abhi-) + नेता (netā).
Borrowed from Sanskrit आन्ध्र (āndhra), from Sanskrit अन्ध्र (andhra).
Borrowed from Classical Persian آبْنُوس (ābnūs), from Middle Persian [script needed] (ʾpnws /⁠abnūs⁠/), from Ancient Greek ἔβενος (ébenos), from Egyptian hbnj (“ebony”). U13:n-Z4:M3

s.g: aarti (a type of worship ritual involving candles)
a female given name, Aarti and Arti, from Sanskrit

ety.text: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit आलस्य (ā́lasya). Doublet of आलस (ālas).

From Sanskrit उन्दुर (undura), इन्दूर (indūra) from a lost Vedic substrate language, likely related to Austroasiatic Munda Languages(compare Old Khmer kuntūra whence Khmer កណ្ដុរ (kɑndol)). Compare Bengali ইঁদুর (ĩdur), Assamese এন্দুৰ (endur), Sylheti ꠃꠘ꠆ꠖꠥꠞ (undur), Gujarati ઉંદર (undar), Marathi उंदीर (undīr), Konkani उंदिर (undir).

s.g: Kartika (eighth month of the Hindu lunar calendar)
a male given name from Sanskrit

ety.text: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit कार्त्तिक (kārttika), a vṛddhi derivative of कृत्तिका (kṛttikā, “cutter”), a variant of कृतिका (kṛtikā), from the root कृत् (kṛt, “to cut”).

s.g: Kulthi, the horse gram (Macrotyloma uniflorum) (a type of bean eaten in South Asia)

ety.text: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit कुलत्थ (kulattha). Doublet of कुलथी (kulthī) and कुलत्थिका (kulatthikā).

s.g: A river in northern India, tributary of the Ganga, flowing through Uttar Pradesh.
a female given name, Gomati and Gomti, from Sanskrit

ety.text: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀙𑀢𑁆𑀢 (chatta), from Sanskrit छत्र (chatra, “parasol, umbrella”). Doublet of छाता (chātā).
Inherited from Prakrit 𑀛𑀓𑁆𑀔𑀺𑀅 (jhakkhia), conflated with Prakrit *𑀛𑀓𑁆𑀓 (*jhakka, “obstinacy”).
A Sanskritic compound of त्याग (tyāg, “leaving, abandonment”) + पत्र (patra, “letter, paper”).

s.g: Trailokya, the three worlds (the sky, atmosphere and earth; heaven, earth, and the lower regions)

ety.text: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit त्रिलोक (triloka). By surface analysis, त्रि- (tri-) + लोक (lok).
Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀤𑀸𑀲 (dāsa), from Sanskrit दास (dāsá).

s.g: one versed in law, a jurist

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian پنجه (panja). Doublet of पाँच (pā̃c, “five”).
Borrowed from Northwestern Indo-Aryan, whence also Punjabi ਪੰਜਾ (pañjā), from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀧𑀁𑀘𑀕 (paṃcaga), from Sanskrit पञ्चक (pañcaka, “set of 5”). Cognate with Nepali पन्जा (panjā).
Borrowed from Sanskrit परिहार्यता (parihāryatā). By surface analysis, परिहार्य (parihārya) + -ता (-tā).
Compound of पर्वत (parvat, “mountain”) + रोही (rohī, “one who climbs”).

s.g: A field that is ploughed and left uncultivated in monsoon or autumn to prepare it for sowing the rabi (spring) crop; fallow land.

ety.text: From Sanskrit परिहर (parihara, “leaving out, omission”), from परिहृ (parihṛ, “to leave”). Compare परिहरना (pariharnā, “to abandon”), परिहार (parihār, “avoidance”).
From the oblique masculine form of पहला (pahlā, “first”).

x: मैं सरकारी प्रेस पे काम करता हूँ।

s.g: Phalguna (twelfth month of the Hindu lunar calendar)

ety.text: Borrowed from Sanskrit फाल्गुन (phālguna), from फल्गुन (phálguna, “the red one”), from फल्गु (phalgú, “reddish”).

s.g: a name for Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi
to be extinguished (as of a fire, light)
to be cooled, slaked (as of hot iron, lime)
to be relieved (as of hunger, thirst)
to be calmed (as of agitated feelings)

to be subdued (as of the emotions or the voice)

Borrowed from Sanskrit रुचिमत (rucimata). By surface analysis, रुचि (ruci) + -मान (-mān).

to cause wrinkles to appear, wrinkle up; to crumple

ety.text: Hindi verb set सिकुड़ना (sikuṛnā) सिकोड़ना (sikoṛnā) Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀲𑀁𑀓𑁄𑀟𑀺𑀬 (saṃkoḍiya, “contracted”), from Sanskrit सं-कोटयति (saṃ-koṭayati).
Back-formation from सुट्टा मारना (suṭṭā mārnā, “to smoke a cigarette”), itself borrowed from Punjabi ਸੂਟਾ ਮਾਰਨਾ (sūṭā mārnā, “to smoke violently”), from ਸੂਟਾ (sūṭā, “violent inhalation (of smoke)”).
Learned borrowing from Sanskrit सौभाग्य (sáubhāgya). Doublet of सुहाग (suhāg).
